skills.name: The financial position of a business: definition and evaluation

note.text:
The financial position (financial situation) of a business is the state of what it owns and what it owes at a given date.
• What it owns: its resources, called assets (premises, equipment, vehicles, goods, money owed by customers, cash and bank).
• What it owes: to outsiders (liabilities, such as loans and unpaid suppliers) and to the owner (capital, or owner's equity).
Evaluating the financial position means listing each asset and each debt and giving it a value in money (FCFA) at that date.
The financial position changes every time the business makes a transaction, so it is always stated on a particular date: “as at 31 December 2026”.

worked_example.problem: Mme Ekwe's shop has goods worth {s} FCFA, equipment worth {e} FCFA and cash of {c} FCFA. She owes the bank {l} FCFA. Evaluate what she owns and what she owes.
steps: What she owns (assets): {s} + {e} + {c} = {s + e + c} FCFA.
The rest belongs to her (capital): {s + e + c} − {l} = {s + e + c - l} FCFA.
worked_example.answer: Owns {s + e + c} FCFA; owes {l} FCFA; capital {s + e + c - l} FCFA.

cards.idea: The financial position is what a business owns and what it owes, on a given date.
example: Owns: assets. Owes: liabilities and capital.

cards.idea: Evaluating means giving each item a value in money (FCFA).
The financial position is always stated at a particular date, because it changes with every transaction.

pick.q: Why is the financial position always given at a particular date?
pick.y: Each sale or purchase changes it.

pick.q: What does evaluating the financial position mean?
pick.r: listing what is owned and owed and giving each a money value
pick.y: Each item gets a value in FCFA.

A business has premises worth {p} FCFA, goods worth {g} FCFA and cash of {c} FCFA. What is the total value of what it owns?
solution: Add the values of everything it owns.

questions.prompt: A business owns items worth {a} FCFA in total and owes outsiders {l} FCFA. How much belongs to the owner?

misconceptions.explain: Subtract what is owed to outsiders.

solution: What belongs to the owner is what is owned minus what is owed to outsiders.
